# bearmq_queue (Resource)

A queue inside a BearMQ virtual host. Every argument forces replacement — BearMQ queues are immutable once declared.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bearmq_vhost" "orders" {
  name = "orders-prod"
}

# Dead-letter target.
resource "bearmq_queue" "paid_dead" {
  vhost_id = bearmq_vhost.orders.id
  name     = "orders.paid.dead"
  durable  = true
}

# Work queue: 60s TTL, dead-letters into orders.dlx.
# Numeric-looking argument values are sent to the broker as JSON numbers.
resource "bearmq_queue" "paid" {
  vhost_id = bearmq_vhost.orders.id
  name     = "orders.paid"
  durable  = true
  dlq_name = bearmq_queue.paid_dead.name

  arguments = {
    "x-message-ttl"             = "60000"
    "x-dead-letter-exchange"    = "orders.dlx"
    "x-dead-letter-routing-key" = "orders.paid.dead"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Queue name, unique within the virtual host.
- `vhost_id` (String) ID of the owning virtual host.

### Optional

- `arguments` (Map of String) AMQP `x-` arguments. Numeric/boolean-looking values are sent as JSON numbers/booleans (e.g. `x-message-ttl = "60000"`). Not refreshed from the server.
- `auto_delete` (Boolean) Delete the queue once its last consumer disconnects. Defaults to `false`.
- `dlq_name` (String) Name of a dead-letter queue to attach.
- `durable` (Boolean) Survive a broker restart. Defaults to `true`.
- `exclusive` (Boolean) Restrict the queue to its declaring connection and delete it when that connection closes. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `actual_name` (String) Internal storage name assigned by BearMQ.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `max_message_count` (Number) Configured max message count.
- `overflow_policy` (String) Overflow policy reported by BearMQ.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status reported by BearMQ.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Queues import as "<vhost_id>/<queue_id>".
terraform import bearmq_queue.paid 7f3c1e90-0c2a-4b1d-9f4e-1a2b3c4d5e6f/b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f0123456789a
```
